<header class="dg-head dg-head-chapter"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 4</p><h1 class="dg-title">Tangent Spaces</h1></header>
<div class="dg-motivation"><div class="dg-motivation-title">Motivation: Vectors without arrows</div><div class="dg-motivation-upper"><p>In <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^d\)</span>, a vector <span class="math inline">\(v\)</span> at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> is an arrow from <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> to <span class="math inline">\(p + v\)</span>. On a manifold this picture is unavailable, since points cannot be added and there is no ambient space for the arrows to live in. What survives is the action of <span class="math inline">\(v\)</span> on functions. In <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^d\)</span>, along the curve <span class="math inline">\(\gamma(\lambda) = p + \lambda v\)</span>,  <span class="math display">\[
        (f \circ \gamma)'(0) = v^i \, \partial_i f(p) ,
    \]</span>  and choosing for <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span> the coordinate functions recovers every component <span class="math inline">\(v^i\)</span>. Curves and smooth functions both make sense on a manifold, so this action can serve as the definition of a vector.</p>
</div><div class="dg-motivation-lower">
<p><strong>Goal.</strong> Build, at every point <span class="math inline">\(p \in \mathcal{M}\)</span>, the vector spaces of Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../vector-spaces/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Vector_Spaces">2</a>.</p>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>Define the <strong>tangent space</strong> <span class="math inline">\(T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span> as the set of velocities of curves through <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, acting on scalar fields as directional derivatives, and show that it is a <span class="math inline">\(d\)</span>-dimensional vector space.</p></li>
<li><p>Derive, rather than postulate, the chart-induced bases and the transformation laws of components, which distinguish covariant from contravariant objects.</p></li>
<li><p>Construct its dual, the <strong>cotangent space</strong> <span class="math inline">\(T^*_p\mathcal{M}\)</span>, whose elements are the differentials of scalar fields, and the tensor spaces <span class="math inline">\(T^{(r,s)}_p\mathcal{M}\)</span>.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>The four-velocity of a particle is the velocity of its worldline at a point of spacetime, an element of <span class="math inline">\(T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span>.</p></div></div>
